verses.1: After this incident occurred, all the high priests and the elders of the people decided to kill Jesus.
verses.2: And after they had captured him, they handed him over to Pilate the governor.
verses.3: Then Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned as a traitor. So he gave the thirty pieces of silver to the priests and elders.
verses.4: He said, “It’s a sin to give away one’s blood.” They replied, “What does that have to do with us? You see for yourself.”
verses.5: And when he put the silver into the ship, he left it there. Then he went away.
verses.6: But the high priests, after taking the silver, said, “It is not proper to throw it into the pot, for its value lies in its purity.”
verses.7: Taking counsel with them, they decided to use Agron of Kerameos as a burial place for the foreigners.
verses.8: Therefore, that field was named Agros Aïmatos, and it has remained so to this day.
verses.9: Then the promise made by the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled. They received thirty silver coins as payment for being honored among the descendants of Israel.
verses.10: And they brought them to the field of Keraamos, as my master had ordered me to do.
verses.11: And Jesus stood in front of the governor. The governor asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus replied, “You say so.”
verses.12: And he did not respond to the accusations against him by the high priests and elders.
verses.13: Then Pilate says to him, “Do you not hear how many crimes you have committed?”
verses.14: And not a single word was said to him, so that one could not admire the ruler any more.
verses.15: On the Sabbath, the ruler would choose one person from the crowd to be bound in a rope.
verses.16: At that time, they had a special title for this person, which was called Jesus Barabbas.
verses.17: So, Pilate said to them, “What do you want me to do with you? Should I release Jesus of Galilee, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
verses.18: For they knew that they had given him over to hatred.
verses.19: While he was still standing there, his wife rushed towards him and said, “Nothing will happen to you or to justice through him today. After all, many people have suffered because of him.”
verses.20: But the high priests and the elders persuaded the crowd to request that Barabbas be released, while Jesus should be executed.
verses.21: Then the governor replied to them, “What do you want me to dismiss from among you?” They said, “Babaius.”
verses.22: Pilate says to them, “What should I do with Jesus, who is called the Christ?” Everyone says, “He should be crucified.”
verses.23: But he said, “What evil has he done?” They became more aggressive, saying, “He should be crucified.”
verses.24: Seeing that nothing was achieved, but instead more noise was created, Pilate took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. He said, “I am a sinner because of this bloodshed. Now, see.”
verses.25: And when everyone in the crowd spoke, they said, “His blood will be shed upon us and upon our children.”
verses.26: Then he released them from their bonds. After covering Jesus with a cloak, he handed him over to be crucified.
verses.27: Then, the soldiers of the commander took Jesus to the palace, carrying him along with them. They covered all the way there.
verses.28: And when they exposed him to chalybeate iron, they covered him with it.
verses.29: And after placing a crown made of hair on his head, they also placed a crown on his right side. Then, standing in front of him, they praised him, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”
verses.30: And after they had struck him, they put the stick into his head.
verses.31: And when they were singing to him, they removed his clothes from him, and they also put on his clothes. Then they took him away to be crucified.
verses.32: When they came out, they found a man named Cyril. They asked him to carry the cross for them.
verses.33: And when they went to a place called Golgotha, which is the place where Christ was crucified.
verses.34: They gave him drink, which was mixed with honey. But after drinking it, he refused to continue drinking anymore.
verses.35: They also nailed him up, splitting his legs apart and covering them with cloth.
verses.36: And those who were sitting there observed him there.
verses.37: And they wrote down his accusation on top of his head. This man is Jesus, the King of the Jews.
verses.38: At that time, two lances are also used to crucify him; one from the right side, and one from the left.
verses.39: But those who were approaching gestured by moving their heads.
verses.40: And they said, “He who crucified him was also building his house in three days. If you are indeed a son of God, then get off that cross.”
verses.41: Similarly, the high priests, along with the scribes and elders, said the same thing.
verses.42: He saved others, but he himself cannot be saved. He is the king of Israel. Now let us fall down before him and believe in him.
verses.43: I will now try to approach the god; I will do this if he wishes. For he said that I am a son of God.
verses.44: And those who were bound together with him also recognized him as such.
verses.45: And from the sixth hour, darkness covered the entire land, until the ninth hour.
verses.46: And about the ninth hour, Jesus spoke with a loud voice, saying, “Are you really willing to go away? This is what it is: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
verses.47: When they heard what was said there, they said that this man was speaking in the language of Elyas.
verses.48: And immediately, one of them acted, took some grain, fed it to the young ones, and then poured it into a container.
verses.49: But the rest said, “Let’s see if Elyas will come to save him.”
verses.50: And Jesus again cried out with a loud voice, and the spirit left him.
verses.51: And it seemed that the top part of the temple had split from above down to two parts. The ground also split apart, and the stones were scattered everywhere.
verses.52: And the memories were forgotten, and many of the bodies of those who slept in peace were raised from their graves.
verses.53: And after leaving the tombs, they entered the holy city, accompanied by his relics. They were seen by many people.
verses.54: But the hundred men and those who were with them saw Jesus, and when they saw the earthquake and all that happened, they were terrified. They said, “Truly, this man was indeed a son of God.”
verses.55: And there were many women there, whom I saw from a distance. They followed Jesus from Galilee to serve him.
verses.56: In those places lived Mary Magdalene, Mary from the family of Jacob, Joseph’s mother, and also the mother of the sons of Zebedaeus.
verses.57: And because of his vision, a rich man came from Arimathea. His name was Joseph. He too was taught by Jesus.
verses.58: When he came before Pilate, he saw the body of Jesus. At that moment, Pilate ordered that it be handed over.
verses.59: And taking the body of Jesus, he wrapped it in clean linen.
verses.60: And he placed it in the new monument where he was buried. Then, after he placed a large stone at the entrance of the monument, he left.
verses.61: And there was Mary Magdalene and another Mary, both sitting opposite the tomb.
verses.62: At the end of the day, after all preparations were completed, the high priests and the Pharisees gathered together before Pilate.
verses.63: Saying, “Lord, we remember that that man said he would still be alive. I will come back after three days.”
verses.64: Therefore, it is necessary to keep the tomb safe until the third day. Otherwise, when his disciples come and steal it away, they will be punished by God. He will rise from the dead, and then the second layer of bones will be placed over the first layer.
verses.65: Pilatos said to them, “Have you been given a guarantee? Make sure you are safe, as you know.”
verses.66: But those who went there managed to break into the tomb by sealing the stone in place along with the vaulting.
